text:
incident-bot: :loud_sound: PG: prod-west gpu-inference queue growth detected. Queue > 11k for rerank-models. Autoscaler failing to allevate backlog. Alert created 2026-03-15T03:22:08Z.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. Observing queue increase with many pods Pending. GPU util is uneven: some GPUs at 95% while many slices are idle but unusable due to MIG fragmentation.

frank.lee: quick context: last week we added mixed workload tenants to this cluster and some older jobs reserved larger MIG slices (4g/3g). New workloads request 1g slices densely. Scheduler can't binpack them.

gwen-ops: kube-scheduler events: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  1m (x12 over 4m)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient cpu, 4 had no matching MIG resource.
```

sre-oncall: exact node-level error from our custom GPU-scheduler: 
```
2026-03-15T03:24:12Z placement.go:179] placePod pod=rerank-77: no contiguous 1g slices found; node slices=(3g,5g) -> fragment prevents allocation
```

harry-support: customer impact: support dashboard shows ~25 external customers with elevated latency or occasional 503 on text-generation endpoints. A handful of premium customers reported timeouts. Escalating to CSMs.

ivy-prod: mitigation proposals: (A) schedule a rolling defrag: cordon small set of nodes, migrate workloads off, reprovision those nodes with uniform 1g slices; (B) quick route: divert some traffic to fallback small-cpu model for non-critical tiers; (C) change pod requests to allow allocation on 2g slices (runtime shim to split).

sre-oncall: starting with minimal blast radius: pausing autoscaler to stop further failing attempts: `kubectl patch configmap autoscaler -p '{"data":{"enabled":"false"}}'`

eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler paused by sre-oncall at 03:29:10Z. queue=11420, p95=4.6s, error-rate=2.3%.

frank.lee: I'll cordon and drain two most-fragmented nodes and reprovision them to 1g slices. Plan: wave 1: n-gpu-07, wave 2: n-gpu-09. Will keep drains spaced 8 minutes apart.

gwen-ops: drain commands ready: 
```bash
kubectl cordon n-gpu-07 && kubectl drain n-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=45
infractl reprovision --node n-gpu-07 --mig-config=1g:8
```

sre-oncall: handoff: I'm on until 04:00Z. @frank.lee coordinate with @alice.huang for routing changes.

alice.huang: acknowledged. I'll flip a temporary route to send 12% of standard-tier traffic to cpu-fallback to shave tails. Applying route change now.

eng-runtime-bot: routing change applied at 03:36:33Z. queue dips ~7% in 90s.

harry-support: customer comms: letting affected customers know we're investigating and applying mitigations.

frank.lee: wave 1 complete: n-gpu-07 drained and reprovisioned with 1g slices. Rebooted and rejoined cluster. Placement logs show several successful allocations to n-gpu-07.

eng-runtime-bot: metrics at 03:44Z: queue=8800, p95=3.3s, errors=1.4%.

frank.lee: wave 2 starting: cordon n-gpu-09. Will evict tolerant jobs first.

ivy-prod: suggestion: pause quantized-rerank canary; it's increasing concurrency and shrinking batch sizes which exacerbates fragmentation impact.

alice.huang: pausing canary now: `featurectl toggle rerank-quant-v2 off`

eng-runtime-bot: feature flag toggled at 03:49Z.

gwen-ops: after wave 2 reprovision, scheduler placement errors dropped from ~60/min to ~8/min. Still some backlog.

sre-oncall: deploying small scheduler change: allow pods in rerank class to accept 2g slices where runtime can split logical allocations. Pushing canary 5% to start.

eng-runtime-bot: scheduler-split-canary deployed at 03:56Z. Initial placements successful.

frank.lee: good signal: pending pod count decreased and many pods scheduled on newly provisioned homogeneous nodes.

harry-support: update: customer timeouts down 70%. Tickets trending down. CSMs notified.

ivy-prod: next steps: re-enable autoscaler with fragmentation-aware policy and limit step scale to avoid oscillation; file infra ticket to add periodic defrag job and make the autoscaler MIG-shape aware.

sre-oncall: summary of actions: paused autoscaler; drained & reprovisioned two nodes to uniform 1g slices; paused canary; added routing fallback (12%); deployed scheduler shim to accept 2g->1g split for tolerant workloads.

eng-runtime-bot: at 04:10Z metrics: queue=2600, p95=1.4s, errors=0.5%. No new scheduling failures.

frank.lee: filing infra ticket: INFRA-4521 "MIG fragmentation: defrag job + autoscaler enhancements" with proposed fixes (periodic consolidation, autoscaler shape-awareness, scheduler flexible mapping).

gwen-ops: logs and traces stored: s3://redwood-incidents/1969998888/gpu-scheduler-logs.tar.gz

harry-support: drafting customer postmortem; will coordinate with product for messaging.

ivy-prod: once stable, let's capture an ops runbook called "MIG fragmentation response" and include playbook steps and safe limits for rolling reprovision. I'll own the doc.

sre-oncall: handing off to alice.huang at 04:00Z. Left autoscaler paused and two nodes reprovisioned; I'll remain available.

alice.huang: taking over. Will monitor for 1hr then re-enable autoscaler with new policy.

eng-runtime-bot: handoff logged at 04:00:12Z.

--- follow-up (04:45Z) ---

alice.huang: autoscaler re-enabled with `prefer_homogeneous:true` and `max_scale_step:3`. Applied policy.

eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler resumed at 04:46Z. queue=900, p95=0.9s. All clear for now.

frank.lee: RCA notes draft: root cause = MIG fragmentation + workload shift (smaller queries reduced batching) + canary increasing concurrency. Secondary cause = autoscaler not accounting for fragmentation and retrying incompatible instance types. Recommendations: periodic defrag job, autoscaler shape-aware logic, safer rollout gating, scheduler enhancements for flexible slice mapping.

harry-support: customer messages sent at 05:10Z. No SLA credits required. Monitoring continues for 24h.

ivy-prod: thanks team. We'll convert the RCA and mitigation steps into a runbook and infra ticket. Great coordination.
